audit.whatIsWrong: Frost Armor is never mentioned, and four separate lines assume every mushroom Sejuani steps on slows her ("if she walks over one she takes a slow", "every shroom she steps on slows her", "walk up and reveals herself", "she cannot close the gap").
audit.why: Fury of the North (P): after being out of combat Sejuani gains Frost Armor, which grants Armor, Magic Resist AND IMMUNITY TO SLOWS, and it persists for a short time after she takes damage. An approaching, out-of-combat Sejuani takes the mushroom damage and walks straight through the slow. The entire mushroom-wall plan this matchup is built on works at roughly half strength against her, and nothing in either layer says so.
audit.corrected: Frost Armor makes an out-of-combat Sejuani slow-immune — your mushrooms damage her approach, they do not stop it. Force her into combat first.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two Sejuani abilities are assigned to the wrong slots throughout. Permafrost is called her passive (spikes[0] "Sejuani's Permafrost passive", early "her Permafrost passive"), and Fury of the North is called her E (wants.foe[0] "her E Fury of the North stun"). Arctic Assault is called her W in five places (early, wants.you[2], wants.foe[1], whys[1], whys[4]).
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/sejuani.json: P Fury of the North, Q Arctic Assault, W Winter's Wrath, E Permafrost, R Glacial Prison. The passive and the E have been swapped with each other, and her Q has been relabelled as her W. Winter's Wrath — the ability that actually matters most here — is never mentioned at all.
audit.corrected: P Fury of the North, Q Arctic Assault, W Winter's Wrath, E Permafrost, R Glacial Prison.

audit.whatIsWrong: The whole blind plan rests on "she needs only two auto hits to proc her E stun" (whys[0]), "Stack Permafrost with two auto hits" (wants.foe[0]), and "the blind cancels each auto and drops her stacks" (whys[2], mid).
audit.why: Riot's text puts Frost stacks on Winter's Wrath — an ability, not a basic attack. Blind stops basic attacks and nothing else, so blinding Sejuani does not prevent her from arming Permafrost. The entry sells Blinding Dart as the counter to her stun when it is not one; the counter is spacing outside her 600-range W and 650-range Q.
audit.corrected: Winter's Wrath applies the Frost stacks that arm Permafrost, and it is an ability — you cannot blind your way out of the stun.

audit.whatIsWrong: Packet flags zero cooldown-sequencing cues, and the full layer tells the player to "track Permafrost's cooldown".
audit.why: Permafrost is on a 1.5-second cooldown — tracking it is meaningless. The gates that matter are Arctic Assault at 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s (her only gap-close, and an enormous window at rank 1) and Winter's Wrath at 9/8/7/6/5s (the Frost applier). What the player should track is her Frost stack count, not a cooldown.
audit.corrected: Track Frost stacks, not Permafrost. The countable cooldown is Arctic Assault — 18 seconds at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Glacial Prison is described as an "AOE stun" and a "five-man AOE stun" (spikes[3], whys[6]).
audit.why: The bola stuns only the first champion it hits; everyone else caught in the resulting ice storm is slowed, not stunned. That changes the positioning rule from "stay out of the AoE" to the much more actionable "never be the closest champion to her".
audit.corrected: Glacial Prison stuns the first champion hit at 1300 range and slows the rest — do not be the front of the group.

audit.whatIsWrong: Teemo's Q is written "Blinding Shot" in wants.you[0], early and whys[1].
audit.why: champ-data/_kits/teemo.json gives slot Q as "Blinding Dart".

audit.whatIsWrong: mid opens "Levels 4-5 is your takeover. Q is max-ranked".
audit.why: Rank 5 needs level 9, and Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank anyway — ranking it changes damage and blind duration, never availability. There is no cooldown-based takeover at 4-5.
audit.corrected: Blinding Dart is 7s at every rank, so it is up for every trade from level 1 — nothing about its availability changes at 4-5.

audit.whatIsWrong: "Liandry's Angueur" in spikes[2], late and whys[5].
audit.why: Not a real item. Liandry's Torment is the name used in the full layer of this dataset.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers publish opposite level charts for the first two stages. content.win = [Sejuani, Sejuani, Skill, Skill, Teemo, Teemo, Teemo]; full.phases sides = [Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Teemo, Skill, Teemo, Teemo] with ratings 4/10 and 3/10.
audit.why: The content early paragraph argues Sejuani wins the first two levels; the full layer rates the same two stages as Teemo's easiest in the matchup. Both cannot be shown to a player. No edit proposed for the sides: "Sejuani" and "Teemo" cannot be swapped inside the length band.
audit.corrected: Pick one chart. Flagged for the user rather than edited.

edits.before: Sejuani wins the first two levels cleanly — her Permafrost passive means any two basic attacks she lands on you let her E-stun you in place, and at Level 1 your Blinding Shot alone cannot prevent her from walking up and chunking you with her W Arctic Assault knockup. edits.after: Sejuani wins the first two levels cleanly — Winter's Wrath applies the Frost stacks that arm Permafrost, and because it is an ability rather than a basic attack, Blinding Dart does nothing to stop the stun. Play back beyond her range, last-hit with Q, and remember Frost Armor: out of combat she carries bonus armour and magic resist and is immune to slows, so she takes the poke and keeps walking. The moment she burns Arctic Assault to push you off the wave, note it — 18 seconds at rank 1, and the safest window you get to stack E poison.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 is your takeover. Q is max-ranked, so every time she tries to auto you to build Permafrost stacks you blind her and the stacks fall off — she literally cannot proc her E stun without eating a blind first. Start placing mushrooms at the tribush, the lane-side river bush, and directly behind the wave to punish any forward step. At Level 6 you accelerate your shroom line across the river entrance; if she walks over one she takes a slow and your poison begins eating her percent health, and your camouflage lets you reposition freely while she searches for you through a fogged side lane.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 is your window, but not for the reason you would expect. Blinding Dart is a flat 7 seconds at every rank, so it is up for every trade she offers — what it does not do is stop Winter's Wrath from stacking Frost, because a blind only stops basic attacks. Space outside her 600-range W instead. Start placing mushrooms at the tribush, the lane-side river bush, and directly behind the wave, and accept that Frost Armor lets an out-of-combat Sejuani ignore their slow: they are a damage tax on her approach, not a wall. At Level 6 push the shroom line to the river entrance and use camouflage to reposition while she searches a fogged side lane.

edits.before: Liandry's Angueur is the moment this lane is fully decided — her enormous HP pool feeds your percent-health burn, and a single mushroom field between you and her means she cannot close the gap without losing a third of her health to DoT before she arrives. Stay on the side lane where your mushroom coverage is thickest, take towers freely behind a shroom wall, and only group when objectives force it — one R landing on you before you can W away is an instant death.
edits.after: Liandry's Torment is the moment this lane is fully decided — her enormous HP pool feeds your percent-health burn, and a mushroom field between you and her costs a third of her health before she arrives, even though Frost Armor spares her the slow. The danger late is never the 1v1; it is Glacial Prison catching you mid-reposition. Stay on the side lane where your mushroom coverage is thickest, take towers freely behind a shroom wall, and only group when objectives force it — the bola stuns the first champion it hits, so make sure that is never you.

notes:
Sejuani has the worst slot mapping in this slice: Permafrost and Fury of the North are swapped with each other, Arctic Assault is labelled as her W five times, and Winter's Wrath — the ability that applies the Frost stacks the whole matchup revolves around — is never mentioned once in either layer.

Frost Armor's slow immunity is the buried headline. Teemo's standard plan against a slow melee tank is a mushroom wall, and against Sejuani specifically the wall only deals damage; the slow is ignored whenever she approaches out of combat. This is worth checking in other Teemo-vs-tank entries too, since the same "every shroom she steps on slows her" phrasing is likely templated across matchups.
